description: The figure displays two bar charts comparing the performance of probing single layers versus a weighted sum of all layers in two multilingual BERT models: mBERT and XLM-R. The horizontal axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 (the embedding layer) to 12, with an additional category labeled "concat" indicating the concatenation of all layers. The vertical axis shows the "% point difference" in probing accuracy, with negative values indicating that probing the individual layer performs worse than probing the weighted sum of all layers. In the mBERT chart, the bar for layer 0 is the most negative, showing a large drop in performance (approximately -10% points), while the bars for layers 1 and 2 are also significantly negative (around -8% and -7% respectively), with the remaining layers showing progressively smaller negative differences, and the "concat" bar being positive. In the XLM-R chart, the pattern is similar but less extreme: layer 0 and 1 are the most negative (around -9% and -8% respectively), followed by layer 2 at about -7%, and then a gradual improvement towards the "concat" bar, which is positive. The visual comparison highlights that the embedding layer (0) and early layers are particularly suboptimal for probing when used individually compared to the aggregated representation.
